contribution.position: Holding my earlier position. Answering product: it says nobody else sees a reliability problem and treats the axis as settled. That is not supported. artifact:incident-log shows a 30-day error rate of 1.8% against a 0.3% SLO (six times over budget) and two sev2 incidents. The absence of objections from ops and qa does not count as evidence, because their anchors cover other things: artifact:ops-runbook covers deploy and rollback steps, and artifact:test-report covers functional pass/fail (412 passed, 0 failed, 87% coverage). Neither measures production error rate. On qa's claim that risk is contained, a passing test suite shows the change behaves as specified. It does not show that the live error rate will improve or stay flat, so I do not accept it as an answer to the incident history. On cost, artifact:cost-sheet (+3% against a 5% ceiling) is a separate axis and does not bear on reliability. New point since my last turn: the debate has no artifact that links the change to the two sev2 incidents, such as a root-cause analysis, a list of code paths touched, or a canary/error-rate comparison. That gap is the open item, and I am naming it rather than assuming it. Until that evidence exists, reliability stays opposed with evidence still needed.
